sections.h2: Ottumwa and the Des Moines River
sections.html:
Ottumwa is the Wapello County seat in southeastern Iowa, and the Des Moines River cuts the city into a northern and a southern half. The name comes from a Meskwaki word usually rendered as "tumbling waters," a nod to the rapids that once marked the site. A bridge replaced the old ferry by 1875, and South Ottumwa was annexed in the 1880s.

Coal, meatpacking and farm equipment built the town. Ottumwa reached 33,871 residents in 1960, slid to 24,998 by 2000 and recorded 25,529 in 2020. A city that has lost about a quarter of its peak population has a different housing market than a growing one, and prices reflect it.

sections.h2: Local jobs and what they mean for demand
sections.html: JBS Live Pork is the biggest employer with 2,550 jobs, followed by the Ottumwa Community School District at 800 and Ottumwa Regional Health Center at 692. John Deere Ottumwa Works adds 550. With a few large employers carrying the town, a change at one plant or at the school district shows up in local housing demand quickly.

sections.h2: Which side of the river is the house on?
sections.html:
The Ottumwa Community School District serves the city and rural Wapello County, and its elementary schools are grouped by north and south side. Douma and Liberty are on the south side, while James, Horace Mann, Wilson, Eisenhower and Fahrney are on the north. Confirm the attendance zone for the address before you tell a buyer about schools.

U.S. Route 34 and Iowa Highway 149 serve the town, and U.S. 63 bypasses it. Amtrak's California Zephyr stops daily in each direction. Because the river divides the city, tell buyers which side the house sits on and how it connects to the highways. The Ottumwa Transit Authority runs five weekday routes and two Saturday routes, with no Sunday service.

The flood of 1851 damaged the town severely, and the river still bisects the city. Look at drainage and the basement before you list. An owner who can show repair receipts has a clearer story for a buyer. Winters are cold, with an average January high of 32.0 degrees and annual snowfall of 23.6 inches, so roof and heating condition matter too.

sections.h2: Coal, packing plants and older housing
sections.html:
Coal mining began near Ottumwa by 1857, and clay and coal deposits in northeastern Wapello County fed early industry. The John Morrell and Company plant employed workers from 1877 to 1973, and JBS and John Deere carry on that industrial tradition today. Much of the housing stock grew up around those jobs, so many houses are decades old and carry the wear that comes with age.

Indian Hills Community College occupies the former Ottumwa Heights College campus, and Buena Vista University has a regional campus in the city. Both bring students and staff who rent, though a landlord with a worn-out rental may still find few buyers on the open market.

First, we ask for the address and basic facts: who owns it, whether it is occupied, what needs work and whether a mortgage or tax balance is attached. Second, we visit or review photos and run the title. Third, you get an offer in writing that you can take, counter or ignore.

If you accept, the title company opens an escrow file, confirms ownership and orders payoff letters. Closing day is a short signing. The deed goes to the county recorder with a declaration of value, and the transfer tax is handled at that point. Utilities and keys are the last items to settle, and you can ask the closing agent to confirm each step by phone or email before you sign. Sellers who live out of town can usually sign by mail or through a mobile notary.

Landlords in Ottumwa register each rental and have it inspected every three years. Roughly 2,600 units are on the city's list. A rental permit starts with the Rental Permit Application, and the 2025 fee schedule is a separate PDF on the city's site.

The Building and Code Enforcement department, at 105 E. Third Street and 641-683-0650, handles complaints about tall grass and weeds, blighted properties and junk cars. A structure unfit for habitation gets a yellow placard on the front, and nobody may live in it until the violations are corrected. The Health Department posts a list of placarded houses.

Building permits cover most new construction and remodeling and are requested online, along with inspections. The 2015 International Property Maintenance Code is the standard in force. On a placarded house, a cash buyer can still purchase it as-is, but ask the city what has to be fixed before anyone moves in again.

sections.h2: Wapello County property tax and transfer tax
sections.html:
Wapello County collects property tax in two installments, due September 1 and March 1. Each turns delinquent a month later, on October 1 and April 1. Pay at the Treasurer's office in the courthouse at 101 W. 4th Street, or mail a check postmarked by month end to dodge the 1.5 percent penalty. Delinquent interest is 1.5 percent monthly.

Anything still unpaid on May 1 picks up a publication fee and is advertised for the June tax sale. Redeeming costs 2 percent a month in certified funds.

When the deed is presented, the county recorder collects the state transfer tax of $0.80 per $500, exempting the first $500, and takes a declaration of value with it. Of the receipts, 17.25 percent stays with the county and the remainder goes to the state.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or a placard
sections.html: Back taxes come out of your proceeds at closing; ask the Treasurer for the balance before choosing a date. Vacant rentals, inherited houses and placarded houses can all go as-is, but a placard stays on the property until the city approves the repairs.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of an Ottumwa house works
sections.html:
Call with the address and a plain description of the house. After we look it over, a title company drafts the deed and payoff numbers if you take the offer. No lender appraisal holds anything up.

Before closing, pull together the deed, the newest tax bill, any loan payoff details and city notices. You set the date, sign at the title company, and keep what remains after liens and taxes. Repairs and showings never enter the picture, which helps owners facing a placard, an empty rental or an inherited house.

faqs.q: How often are Ottumwa rentals inspected?
faqs.a: Once every three years. About 2,600 rental units are registered with the city.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Ottumwa?
faqs.a: Between 2020 and 2024 the median owner-occupied home was worth $106,300, and gross rent was $921.

faqs.q: When are Wapello County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two installments, September 1 and March 1, each delinquent a month later. Late interest is 1.5 percent monthly.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ottumwa house with a yellow placard?
faqs.a: Usually yes, as-is to a cash buyer, though no one can live in it until violations are corrected. Ask Building and Code Enforcement what is required before reoccupancy.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Ottumwa?
faqs.a: JBS Live Pork with 2,550 jobs, followed by the Ottumwa Community School District at 800.
